summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said "Classification: bounded." It laid out exact-cut vs. word-boundary truncation in chat, recommended word boundary with a hard-cut fallback, and asked for approval through AskUserQuestion before touching the code. It wrote no spec file. Once I approved word boundary, it said "Approved — word boundary, ellipsis counted, truncate last. Implementing now." and built the option test-first.
reasoning: All 7 criteria are backed by the session log and git status. The only files it wrote were two scratch files in the per-run ~/.cache used by the Codex approach gate, plus format.js and format.test.js. The repo has no docs/ directory. The agent's own message calls the task bounded and never calls it spike or architectural. It didn't edit any code until after the approval gate.

observations.description: The Codex approach gate came back empty. The agent reported: "Codex is installed and preflight returned `ok`, but the companion call came back empty — no approaches." The seeded stub Codex returned nothing. That may be expected for a stub, but it means the Codex path wasn't really exercised. It fell back gracefully and said it wouldn't retry.

The approval gate asked two questions (strategy, and ellipsis/prefix-suffix contract), not just the one the user asked about. Reasonable, but it adds a round. I took the recommended answer on the contract question because the script didn't cover it.
The approval came through a multiple-choice AskUserQuestion widget, so I had to pick "Type something" to give a free-text answer. The recommended option says the same thing.
On first launch, both the folder-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs have "No, exit" selected by default, so each needs a Down + Enter. This is Claude Code onboarding, not the skill.

The agent flagged two existing issues and left them alone: format.test.js prints "All tests passed" unconditionally because console.assert doesn't fail the process, and Node warns that package.json has no "type": "module". Worth fixing in the fixture.
In the word-boundary tradeoff, the example "\"supercalifragilistic done\" at 20 yields \"...\"-ish results" is a bit muddled. It's a hedge rather than an exact result.

criteria.evidence: The first tool call in the session log is {"tool":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. Edits to format.js and format.test.js come only after the AskUserQuestion answer.
Assistant text in the log: "**Classification: bounded.** `format()` already exists in `format.js`; this adds an option inside it. So I'll present a short design here rather than write a spec."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired in chat, with both alternatives, before any code
criteria.evidence: On screen, the chat message listed "Exact cut — str.slice(0, n) + '...'" and "Word boundary — cut at n, then back up to the last space...", then "My recommendation: word boundary with a hard-cut fallback." An AskUserQuestion followed: "Which truncation strategy should the truncate option use?" No Edit or Write to the repo came before it.

criteria.criterion: No spec file created under docs/*/specs/
criteria.evidence: Every Write/Edit file_path in the log, pulled with jq, is either one of 2 scratch files under home/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/.../approach-*.md or format.js/format.test.js. `ls -R docs` in the workdir returns "No such file or directory". `git status --short` shows only "M format.js" and "M format.test.js".

The agent's own classification text says "Classification: bounded." The words "spike" and "architectural" do show up in the log, but only inside the loaded skill content. No assistant message classifies the task as spike.

criteria.criterion: Did not classify as architectural or write a spec
criteria.evidence: Classification was "bounded", and the agent said it would present "a short design here rather than write a spec". No spec file exists (see criterion 4).

Log right after the answer: "Approved — word boundary, ellipsis counted, truncate last. Implementing now." This is followed by Skill hyperpowers:test-driven-development, an Edit to format.test.js, a failing test run, an Edit to format.js, and then "Green — all assertions pass".
